texts.firmware.sonic1_rsdk.about: The data file of Sonic the Hedgehog's 2013 remaster: everything the game is. The copy that was checked is the Android release's: in its APK it is assets/Data.rsdk.xmf, which is this file under another name. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.sonic2_rsdk.about: The data file of Sonic the Hedgehog 2's 2013 remaster: everything the game is. The copy that was checked is the Android release's: in its APK it is assets/Data.rsdk.xmf, which is this file under another name. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.property.stage_time_ms: The stage timer (minutes, seconds and hundredths), in milliseconds
texts.setting.devmenu.about: Turns on the engine's developer menu (DevMenu in its settings file), as the decompilation's settings.ini does, and adds a Dev Menu control that opens it (Escape on a PC keyboard). From the menu a stage can be chosen directly. It changes what the game does, so it is part of the project.
texts.setting.game.about: Which game this project plays (it is the System in Chimera): "sonic1" is Sonic the Hedgehog, "sonic2" Sonic the Hedgehog 2, each the 2013 remaster. The game decides which data file the project needs.
texts.setting.language.about: The language of the menus and the game's texts (the engine's Language setting): English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Korean, Chinese (traditional) or Chinese (simplified). The game reads it, so a movie records it.
texts.setting.randomseed.about: The number the engine's random numbers start from. The engine takes it from the clock when it starts (time()); here it is this number, so a movie plays the same every time. A movie records it.
texts.setting.renderscale.about: Draws the picture at once (1) or twice (2) the screen's size each way (the engine's WindowScale setting). At 2 the menus, the 3D title and the touch controls are sharper; the stages are the same pixels made bigger. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.screenwidth.about: How many pixels wide the screen is (the engine's ScreenWidth setting). 424 is upstream's default, a 16:9 screen; 320 is the 4:3 screen of the Mega Drive originals. The width changes how far ahead the player sees and which objects are awake, so it changes the game, and a movie records it.
texts.setting.skipstartmenu.about: Starts the game itself at power-on, without the remaster's start menu (the engine's SkipStartMenu setting): no SEGA and Christian Whitehead screens, no 3D title, no save select. Off by default, as upstream. It changes what the first frames are, so a movie records it.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The game's saves as Emulator > Export Save Data wrote them: SData.bin (the save slots' progress) and SGame.bin, under those names. They are put in place before the game starts, so the game finds them as its own. A file with another name is refused.
